docs.title: Ian-Audio's Wolverine based HiFi System
docs.text:
Welcome to Ian-Audio's Wolverine based HiFi System Design site.

Note this is not official Wolverine documentation.

This documents tailoring a pre and power amplifier, to suit my preferences, needs and constraints.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Objectives
  • Power Selection and Constraints
  • Chassis Fit
  • Wolverine Shared transformer
  • Mezmerise options
  • LED Indicators and Fault Systems

docs.title: Dimensions and characteristics of Cabinet
docs.text:
• Internal width: 505 mm
  • Internal height: 430mm (to underside of shelf above holding CD)
  • Cabinet depth: 450mm
  • Distance from cabinet rear to wall: 65mm (current position)
  • The front of the cabinet has a glass swing door that blocks airflow from the front.
  • The rear of the cabinet has been cut out, so it is open for ventilation.
  • The top turntable shelf thas a rear hole of 50mm and a 4mm gap around the lid perimeter

I'm seeking to get the best out of the speakers, so prefer to go dual mono if I can, to get the better channel separation.

docs.title: Double chassis (separate monoblocs)
docs.text:
With 430mm height in the cabinet, 2 x 3U monoblocs leaves 170mm height for ventilation. That might be distributed as 30mm under the base monobloc, 50mm between them, and 90mm above the top one. It doesn't sound generous.

For airflow, I would support the upper monobloc on a frame above the lower one, rather than a full width and depth shelf. The frame would straddle the lower monobloc, bearing on the cabinet base.

The build guide says "Monoblocks are best reserved for builders who deliberately want separate amplifiers, have room for two chassis, and accept the extra cost and duplicated mains wiring."

I like the idea of the optimal architecture, but it is more work and cost to build, and has the concern that there might not be enough air gap for ventilation. The optimal and usual way to use monoblocs is to put them next to the speakers, but I'm not doing that, so I'd not get much benefit from separate chassis.

It may be fine thermally, partnered with a 50VDC (low heat output) variant of the Wolverine, but I don't know of a way to be sure about it in advance.

docs.title: Single chassis (full Dual Mono - 2 transformers)
docs.text:
A multi-layer build with 2 stacked transformers (true dual mono) should work in principle. The problem is fitting it all in.

It might need a 5u chassis to get the height to fit 2 transformers. The Parker cabinet can accommodate a 5U chassis, leaves 208mm vertical gap, ample for ventilation.

I'd originally thought it would be more difficult than a shared transfomer, but it probably isn't for me. It does mean more mechanical support, but as that's an area I'm strong in, it's not really a risk. Because it uses 2 half size transformers (eg 2 x 400 vA) the floor area is reduced compared to one big one.

I should look more into this.

docs.title: Single chassis (partial dual mono, shared transformer)
docs.text:
The 4U chassis fits in the cabinet with 259mm vertical gap for feet and overhead ventilation, and 27mm to the sides. That's a lot better than 2 chassis - so much space that ventilation doesn't sound like it would be a problem.

The build guide says: "As a practical rule, choose the simplest layout that meets your actual need. A cleanly built shared-supply stereo Wolverine is usually preferable to an overcrowded dual-mono build or a pair of monoblocks built only because they seem more impressive."

I don't want to be overcrowded, but want to explore the options for dual rather than going straight for a stereo build. One way to get more space is to use a shared transformer, with independent windings. That isnt true mono, but saves a lot of chassis base space, and probably gets most of the dual mono benefits. It means a custom transformer, so there will be a cost penalty. So far I've focused on this one.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Top fixed (turntable) shelf of cabinet: MNX10 Streamer and Preamp (side by side).
  • Second shelf: CD player
  • On base of Cabinet: Stereo Wolverine power amp

docs.title: Wolverine Chassis Details (assuming partial dual mono, shared transformer )
docs.text:
• Modushop Dissipante 4U, 400mm depth Black.
  • Front 10mm aluminium, aluminium covers.
  • Width 450mm, height = 171mm (without feet)
  • The standard "Deluxe diyAudio" rear plate would suit me very well.

docs.title: Preamp Chassis
docs.text:
I will use a Modushop Galaxy 2U half width chassis for the Preamp (height = 80mm) This fits the Mezmerize PCB intended for this chassis (200.5 × 68.6 mm) with enough extra depth to facilite a neat build

  • Modushop Galaxy 2U, 230mm wide x 280mm depth Black
  • Front 10mm aluminium, aluminium covers, height = 80mm (without feet)
  • The preamp and streamer will fit side by side with 60mm gap. (Cabinet 450mm, MXN10 215 mm wide)

docs.title: LED displays and Fault methodology
docs.text: A 12V trigger system was originally considered, but later rejected as it adds complexity without sound benefit. The preamp and power amplifiers will be housed in a cabinet so they won't be far apart - it is easy to acccess them to turn them on individually. So the power and LED methodology can be simple and old school.

docs.title: Mezmerize preamp
docs.text:
• On-off push button (illuminated red ring) latching on front panel.
  • Not too bright, I'm sitting opposite
  • Remains depressed when on, so tactile.
  • Main use as a visual prompt/reminder to turn it off sound system not in use.
  • No fault detection in preamp
  • IEC connector in rear, incorporating suitably rated fuse.
  • No switch at rear.

docs.title: Protection Philosophy
docs.text:
Protect it as fully as practical, but minimise external displays.

Fault display on the front panel would be good in some ways, but I'd hope to not need it. It adds to build complexity. So:

  • There is no fault display on the front panel.
  • But protection is given for speaker "out" over-voltage, over-current (speaker protection board)
  • Over-temperature protection is given via the speaker protection board - e.g using 75 C NC bimetal thermal switches atttached to the heatsinks.
  • If the heatsink temperature exceeds the defined protection threshold, the amplifier output is disabled and a dedicated LED fault indicator appears on the internal board.
  • If the speaker protection fault triggers, the amplifier output is disabled and a dedicated LED fault indicator appears on the internal board.
  • If the amp is systemically not operating normally after a cool down, I go into diagnostics mode, take the cover off, power up and look to see which internal fault LED lights under power.

docs.title: Power Control
docs.text:
• The primary purpose of the LED in the front panel push button is to tell me the amp is on, reminding me to turn it off if I am not using it.
  • A front-panel push button (latched ) controls amplifier operation via the soft-start circuit.

An IEC inlet with integral fuse is fitted to the rear panel. No rear-panel power switch is required, as the amplifier will be installed within a cabinet where rear access is limited. The switch would simply be on all the time However, if I'm using the Deluxe chassis, I'd need to use one with a rear panel switch so the IEC unit fits the cutout.

docs.title: Status Indication
docs.text:
• On-off push button (illuminated red ring), latched, on front panel.
  • Not too bright, I'm sitting opposite.
  • Remains depressed when on, so tactile.
  • The LED extinguishes whenever the amplifier is switched off.
  • If the button is depressed, illuminated, but there is no sound when playing music, a fault of some kind has occurred.

docs.title: Mezmerize preamp Options
docs.text:
• Mezmerize standard '10 years after' B1 buffer PCB, running 200 mA,
  • Chassis Modushop Galaxy 2U, 230mm wide x 280mm depth. Aluminium cover.
  • Provision for 3 line level audio inputs (CD, NET, and AUX)
  • Rotary switch for input with 60 deg throw; Greyhill 50D60-01-1-AJN (6.35mm shaft)
  • Input Knob Modushop 25mm black. (drill out to fit 6.35mm)
  • Push Button On off, latching, EAO series 82-5151.2116. 19mm, Illuminated Red ring (230VAC for LED)
  • 5 pairs RCA connectors with integrated Teflon or POM isolation washers. eg Neutrik REAN NYS367 (3 input pairs, 2 pair outputs to power amp & sub)
  • Toroidal transformer 50 VA, 2 × 15 V
  • LSK170 transistors - prematched Linear systems 8-11 mA Quad set from diyAudio store. (plus 6 others that don't need to be matched)
  • IEC mains input, flange mount with integrated fuse holder Schurter 4304.6020
  • T315 mA slow blow fuses
  • Potentiometer TKD 2CP-2511 (20kΩ Logarithmic)
  • Volume knob - Modushop 40mm black.
  • Print colour D0D0D0 in RGB - light silver.

docs.title: Site Objective
docs.text:
• To document the thinking process behind my amplifier system design
  • To let others access this so they can help my design if they so wish
  • Let others know how I've been thinking - whether this might help them I don't yet know.

docs.title: Amplifier Objective
docs.text:
To restore the musicality I experienced from the 100W amplifier (now no longer operating) that my neighbour designed and built for me years ago, specifically tailored to my VAF i91 speakers.

To surpass the fall-back amplifier that I am currently using, my Exposure Super XV (40W).

docs.title: Key objectives and constraints:
docs.text:
• Preamp (Mezmerize) plus power amp(s)
  • Approach: "if it is worth doing, it is worth doing well"
  • Timeline: Goal 12 months but no hard limit.
  • Budget: Ample, no hard limit.
  • Partner with VAF i91 mk1 loudspeakers and deliver their full potential, as far as practicable. (nominal impedance 6Ω, sensitivity 88 dB/W/m)
  • On preamp, provide 3 line inputs, one for my MXN10 streamer (NET), my CD player (CD), and a spare (AUX).
  • Build a reliable premium well engineered system, avoiding excessive complexity.
  • Professional level finish - low key, unobtrusive.
  • Avoid domestic disharmony, fit all HiFi chassis into our Parker HiFi cabinet (space for amps 430mm (h) x 505mm (w) x 450mm (d) - open back so ample depth to wall behind)
  • Speakers are close to cabinet (2m cables)
  • I like the idea of dual mono if possible, no fixed constraint on how that might be done.

docs.title: Secondary Objectives
docs.text:
Be compatible with the sorts of upgrades that might happen (though not likely in the short term):

  • SEAS-NEXTEL-2F speakers (semi-active or passive). Impedance: 4-8 Ohms, Sensitivity: 88 dB/W/m
  • Upgrade my streamer (MXN10), possibly to something that supports Dirac live room correction such as a Bluesound Node Icon

Neither of these are likely to change the power amplifier needs, but a second output pair on the preamp might be needed.

docs.title: Personal Objectives
docs.text: Now that I am retired, this project lets me engage again with the technical thinking that has always felt satisfying. Whilst I have an engineering background, it isn't in electronics, so this project will give me a challenge.

docs.title: Why the Wolverine Topology
docs.text:
• My VAF i91 speakers are said to benefit from an amplifier that maintains composure and grip.
  • The Wolverine amplifier combines technical excellence with musicality so should be able to deliver that.

docs.title: Why the Mezmerize B1 Buffer Pre‑Amplifier
docs.text:
• The Mezmerize B1 TYA (ten years after) delivers a clean signal with good impedance behaviour
  • It is expected to complement the Wolverines.

docs.title: 1. Amplifier options
docs.text:
My HiFi is currently housed in a Parker cabinet,

For domestic harmony, I need to maintain or improve the look of the lounge room.

I haven't found a better alternate so the amplifier must go in the existing Parker cabinet.

The DiyAudio forums contain many cautions about placing Wolverine amplifiers in cabinets, and comments on the unpredictability of cooling depending on the exact placement.

The cabinet has an open back, but airflow is restricted so the Wolverine amplifier variant selected must be of relatively low heat output.

docs.title: 2. Power match with VAF i91 speaker
docs.text:
I am upgrading to a Wolverine in search of improved sound quality rather than volume.

My VAF signature i91 mk1 speakers have nominal impedance 6Ω, and sensitivity 88 dB/W/m, max 150W.

My 40W per channel Exposure Super VX integrated amp drives these with ample volume for me; I listen at modest levels.

All Wolverine listed options are 100W or more, so I will have more than enough sound level (volume) capability.

I'm upgrading for hoped gains in sound quality, not sound level (volume). The reason to have a bit more is headroom for dynamics.

docs.title: 3. Selection of Wolverine EF3-n model and rail voltage
docs.text:
The Wolverine amplifier comes in variants EF3-3, EF3-4 and EF-3-5. I select the EF3-3 variant as it generates the least heat.

I also must select rail voltage. Higher rail voltages increase output capability, but also generate more heat.

The build guide gives this advice for 2 channels at 4 ohms (rearranged and culled to ignore high power variants)

DC rail Typical VA 8Ω power W AC V 49 500 100 35 49 600 120 35 54 600 120 38 54 700 150 38 57 700 150 40 57 800 160 40 59 800 160 42

But 50V DC / 36 V AC with 600 VA seems enough.

However, I note that the Toroidy 800vA is the same size as the 600vA, so I might pick 36 V AC with 800 VA

One complexity is deciding what voltage of primary should be specified, based on my mains supply. I've been measuring my mains supply for the past week, at different times of day. So far, it ranges from 230V AC to 240V AC. Mornings 230V, evenings 240V. I believe this is on the lower end of typical for Australian supply. So my choices for spec'ing the tranformer primary are 230V, 240V or a custom 235V. I'll get slightly different resulting actual rail voltages depending on which I choose.

I also have to pick the configuration, stereo, dual mono with 2 transformers in a single chassis, or 2 monoblocs

The pre-build guide says:

  • For most builders, a conventional two-channel stereo amplifier in one chassis with one power supply is the best starting point. It is cheaper, simpler, easier to package, and fully adequate for normal home hi-fi.
  • Dual mono is worth considering if you specifically want stronger channel separation, have the chassis space and budget, and are comfortable planning two supply systems inside one enclosure.
  • Monoblocks are best reserved for builders who deliberately want separate amplifiers, have room for two chassis, and accept the extra cost and duplicated mains wiring.
  • If this is your first large amplifier build, choose a conservative configuration. Avoid high rail voltages, unnecessarily complex dual mono layouts, ... A clean, moderate, standard build is much more likely to succeed ...

Monoblocs are marginal in the cabinet regarding remaining gap for ventilation.

Dual mono is complex, but I like the idea of the better channel separation, and don't mind the extra cost, so I think I'll try that despite it being my first amplifier. It better fits the objective of getting the best out of my VAF i91's, as far as practicable.

If I go for a dual mono with shared transformer, I'd pick 1 x 800 VA. If I go for 2 independent transformers, I'd go for 2 x 400 VA.

docs.title: Mitigation for systemic overheating - Wolverine
docs.text:
I've decided to sell my turntable (Linn LP12 with SME IV arm), as I'm no longer using it. This gives more ventilation space in the cabinet (which has an open back)

I will build the preamp as a half width unit, so it can go in the turntable space with my half-width streamer. This leaves a bigger free space for the power amplifier below.

Other things I might try if needed are:

  • Move the cabinet forward to increase the gap at the wall from 65mm to something bigger.
  • Moving the cabinet door forwards by putting the hinges on pads, to create a 10 mm perimeter gap.
  • Removing the cabinet's glass door. (subject to the domestic harmony test)
  • Fan blowing upwards from the base of the cabinet past the amplifiers (last resort)

docs.title: Preamp Power Requirements
docs.text:
I plan to build a standard "10 years after" Mezmerize.

This is designed to run at 200mA and the official Salas BOM nominates a 50vA , 2 x 15 V transformer.

The intended placement in the turntable area has limited ventilation. If it gets too hot, the cabinet top lid gap can be increased.

docs.title: Wolverine shared transformer option
docs.text:
This is a high level summary of the main features being considered (assumes the dual mono shared transformer configuration)

This is more a snapshot, rather than locked in stone - it has been changing as I learn things.

  • EF3-3 with 50V DC rails.
  • 10kΩ input configuration.
  • Dual mono, single chassis build.
  • 800 VA custom transformer with a 4 x 36V AC 192 VA and 2 x 12V 10vA independent secondaries
  • Chassis Modushop Dissipante 4U, 400mm depth, DIY audio Deluxe version
  • 2 x Speaker protection boards (wolverine option monitoring short circuits and managing the 65°C thermal warning loop). go for Mosfet version of parts.
  • Power speaker protection boards from separate regulated 12VDC auxiliary PSU's, each fed from a 12VAC transformer auxiliary winding
  • 2 x 12V dc power regulator module for speaker board e.g Kiro&Seeu 7812-MD-1P
  • 2 x Ground lift boards (wolverine option)
  • 2 x T-Ground boards (wolverine option)
  • PSU undecided. 2 stacked diyAudio PSU v3 boards does fit but is bulky, has the caps closer to the sensitive bits than I'd like. Doesnt seem right. look for alternatives
  • Caps: If using two PSU v3 boards, 16 x 4700 uF 35mm Ø x 30mm high Nichicon LLS 80V rated (75200 uF total)
  • thermal Safety Switches: One TO-220 style bimetallic switch per heatsink (e.g 65°C NC Sensata / Airpax 67L065 for the Wolverine board).
  • Soft start: Hypex (purchased, in transit)
  • IEC mains input, flange mount with integrated fuse holder Schurter e.g 4304.6020
  • 4A Slow-Blow (Time-Delay / "T" rated) 5x20mm fuse.
  • Push Button On off, latching, illuminated red ring, e.g EAO 82-5151.2113 (12V LED) or E-Switch PV4F23011-3R4
  • Output transistors, Onsemi 6 x NJW0281G and 6 x NJW0302G from Mouser (but buy 8 pairs)
  • 2 RCA connectors, insulated
  • 4 speaker binding posts
